pairs.claim: Proven subject-change attempt leaves the valid target's result unchanged; only the rejection diagnostic is added
Proven record-type-change attempt leaves the valid target's result unchanged
Proven cross-source correction leaves the valid target's result unchanged
Proven cross-local-ID correction leaves the valid target's result unchanged
A gap stated for another subject is irrelevant, and the boundary attempt it might be confused with does not change the result
Permuting occurrences changes neither variant identities, order nor result

historyResolution.claim: A valid, unambiguous correction resolves the revision-1 payload conflict (history kept as a diagnostic); unresolved authority, an independent active defect, a later revision without supersedes, or ownership-conflicted variants do not
An authorized retraction of the competing branch makes the fork historical; an unauthorized retraction or one with unresolved authority does not

When a now-historical payload conflict suppressed the step 5 fork, two surviving heads with no active defect are a fallback Fork; an authorized retraction of one head resolves it, an unauthorized retraction or one with unresolved authority does not

contrasts.claim: Proven cross-boundary correction (rejected, Known) versus correction identity undeterminable (Unresolved Missing)
Proven unauthorized versus authority missing versus authority malformed
Proven subject change versus subject undeterminable
Boundary rejection of a distinct revision versus a genuine payload conflict under one RevisionRef
A conflict superseded by a valid correction is historical; with an undeterminable correction it still affects the result
An authorized retraction also makes the payload conflict historical; the key becomes Retracted

Retracting a correction whose authority is unknown keeps the supersession uncertainty (Unresolved, possible {@1, excluded}); with known authority the key is Retracted (no reinstatement), and with known lack of authority @1 is Current
A fork recorded at step 5 and the step 7 fallback fork give the same result; only the historical PayloadConflict differs

With retraction authority missing, a step 5 fork stays active (Missing, Conflicting); when the fork was suppressed by a now-historical conflict, the active retraction defect stands alone and the fallback adds no Fork (Missing)
Retracting every surviving head leaves the key Retracted; a superseded revision, conflicted or not, is never reinstated
A well-formed code outside the expansion in a covered system is OutOfDomain (Missing, no candidate); an empty code is malformed, so candidacy is Unresolved{Invalid}, never established nonmembership
A whitespace-only code is malformed (Invalid); a code with surrounding whitespace is well-formed, compared without trimming, and therefore OutOfDomain
An absent concept component is Missing (FieldAbsent); a present null component is malformed (Invalid, CodeMalformed)
